verdict.reason: The diff wraps every list-level gesture in doc.batch() explicitly so the subtree moves as one undo unit (editor.ts:3595-3638, comment: "A single Cmd+Z would then leave the subtree half-moved"; text-editor.ts:2703/2763/2780; text-box-editor.ts:1168-1190), yet no test exercises that grouping through a gesture. Repo-wide, the only test callers of indent/outdent/handleTab are editor-tab-bullet.test.ts, editor-on-cursor-move.test.ts and text-box-editor.test.ts. editor-tab-bullet.test.ts has zero matches for undo/snapshot/canUndo/batch; the new text-box subtree case (text-box-editor.test.ts:550-585) asserts only committed listLevel values; and that file's only undo reference is a smoke test at :351-356 (typeof api.undo is a function, does not throw). Batch-as-one-undo-unit IS covered at the store layer (memory.test.ts:237-345, yorkie-doc-store.test.ts:680-930) and at the Document delegation layer (document.test.ts:1062-1091), but none of those runs an indent gesture, so none would catch the wrapper or the docStore.snapshot() placement regressing at the call site. Repo-wide greps for "one undo|single undo|undo unit|undo step" across test files, and for 1050|half-moved, surface no list-level undo test; the task's own plan (20260908-docs-list-level-subtree-todo.md:51) enumerates the intended tests and undo grouping is not among them. If the batching regresses, one Cmd+Z leaves the parent at its child's level - the exact #1050 corruption - with the suite green, so the gap is major rather than contained.

mergedFrom.summary: No test asserts that one indent/outdent gesture is a single undo unit, though wrapping in `doc.batch()` is a headline behavior change of this diff

finding.summary: The diff's headline structural change — wrapping indent/outdent in `doc.batch()` so a multi-block subtree move is ONE undo unit — has no test in any of the three editors
finding.evidence: editor.ts, text-editor.ts and text-box-editor.ts all gained `doc.batch(() => { snapshot(); applyListLevelChanges(...); ... })` with long comments claiming "one Cmd+Z would leave the subtree half-moved" without it. No added test presses undo. `grep -n undo packages/docs/test` returns hits in memory.test.ts, editor-page-setup.test.ts ('a page-setup change is one undo step'), table-cell-style-guard.test.ts, text-box-editor.test.ts:351 ('exposes undo and redo' — only asserts typeof/not.toThrow) — none over indent/outdent. The seam is demonstrably testable (editor-page-setup.test.ts:159 does exactly this pattern with `editor.undo()`), so nothing prevents a regression that drops or misplaces the batch: a user's Cmd+Z would then leave a list subtree half-moved, and under Yorkie a peer would observe the parent-at-child-level state the change exists to remove.

verdict.reason: The batching change is real (editor.ts:3605/3624, text-editor.ts:2703/2763/2780, text-box-editor.ts:1170/1188) and I found no test anywhere in the repo that exercises undo across an indent/outdent gesture. editor-tab-bullet.test.ts (read in full) asserts only resulting listLevel values, painted x, and cell/header scoping; it has zero undo/batch/snapshot references. Only 11 docs test files call undo() and none mentions indent/listLevel; text-box-editor.test.ts:351 is a typeof/not.toThrow smoke test and its list test at :550 never undoes. The batch() seam is tested only with insertText/applyStyle (store/memory.test.ts:237-283, frontend yorkie-doc-store.test.ts:684-845), never through the list gesture, so nothing would fail if the batch wrapper were dropped or misplaced. Comparable one-undo-step assertions already exist in this suite (editor-page-setup.test.ts:159, edit-link-in-place.test.ts:392), so the gap is fillable. No e2e suite exists and no test spies on batch for a docs editor. Impact is user-visible: a regression yields a half-undone list subtree, and under Yorkie a peer observing the parent-at-child-level state the change exists to remove.
